entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 2132069633148965888: position at J2016.0. Distance: Gaia DR3 parallax 4.5538 +/- 0.5562 mas (same row, RUWE 19.14): 219.60 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): 2.635, -16.375 mas/yr. Radial velocity from No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 2132069633148965888 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 70,000 of its distance per century.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 0.48 +/- 0.066 solar radii from Barclay et al. 2015, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of Kepler-296 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809....7B/abstract). Mass 0.498 +/- 0.067 solar masses from Barclay et al. 2015, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of Kepler-296 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2015ApJ...809....7B/abstract). Temperature 3740 +/- 130 K from Barclay et al. 2015, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of Kepler-296 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive.

entries.subject: Colour
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 3,740 K, because no archive holds a spectrum of this star (stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number), through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffcd98. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: no HD number in SIMBAD; gaia-xp: Gaia DR3 published no sampled BP/RP spectrum of it; pulkovo: no HR number; kiehling: no HR number; kharitonov: no HR number; burnashev: no HR (BS) number; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 3,740 K and log g 4.77 (u1 0.386, u2 0.363): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.
